recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. Do not make broad source edits under FHIR-5497; future changes to individual note/comment fields should be handled under element-specific work-group trackers or the already represented FHIR-7622 family.
issue_request: The Published/Persuasive DSTU1 MnM ballot issue asked for consistent naming and explanation of free-text comment/note fields across resources, including how those fields differ from Resource.text and whether clinical resources should use a singular note element for additional information.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-5497 was found. The Jira resolution says the original methodology proposal was superseded by FHIR-7622. FHIR-7622 was applied in git-svn commit e86f20cfb9b7f9336b4463ff3ee5f44691a937bf, which added the Annotation datatype and active fhir.ini registration.
additional_context: FHIR-7622 replaced the older free-text/string convention with a structured Annotation datatype and note/comment naming guidance. Current source/fhir.ini actively lists Annotation as a normative datatype and tracks historical plural-to-singular renames such as Condition.notes to Condition.note and Procedure.notes to Procedure.note. The combined branch already contains a separate FHIR-7622 audit commit, so FHIR-5497 should not duplicate that superseding issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current build source is already correct for FHIR-5497 when interpreted through FHIR-7622; adding the older methodology text to the Narrative page would duplicate or partially revive superseded DSTU1 wording rather than fix a current semantic problem.

related_jiras.note: FHIR-5497's resolution explicitly says it was superseded by this later Published issue defining Annotation and note/comment guidance.
Later Resolved - No Change issue rejected renaming note elements to annotation, supporting the current singular note convention.

evidence_items.summary: Annotation defines author[x] 0..1, time 0..1, text 1..1, plus guidance about narrative inclusion and non-computable modifying information; Narrative permits generated and human-edited additional information within resource scope.
evidence_items.learned: The current source explains how note-like content relates to narrative without needing the superseded wording restored.
